catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Current NCCP source reconciled; independent clinical/pharmacy approval pending

retrospective_audit_v08440.scope: Bounded repeat audit of existing shared ICI assessment; does not establish new melanoma service completion. Current NCCP thresholds, recovery, recurrence and phase/schedule boundaries checked.
findings: Suspected SJS/TEN had no executable cessation/referral pathway before confirmation; added discontinue/referral, retaining confirmed permanent stop.
Maintenance switch interval text was not executable: added source 14/28-day early-dose guards and missing-timing review; first-maintenance and indication-specific formulation rules unchanged.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist or other appropriately authorised specialist named in the current NCCP source.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Use the most restrictive applicable component rule and confirm dose changes against the current official NCCP PDF.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding includes NCCP 00551 version 7a. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.
clinical_governance.melanoma_unlicensed_posology: NCCP 00551 p 13 footnotei: nivolumab 3 mg/kg with ipilimumab 1 mg/kg is unlicensed melanoma dosing posology in Ireland. Inform/consent patient and ensure D&T/equivalent acknowledgement under hospital policy; preserve distinction from nivolumab 1/ipilimumab 3 regimen 00431.

indications.description: Adult metastatic dMMR/MSI-H colorectal cancer after prior fluoropyrimidine-based combination chemotherapy.
First-line treatment of adult patients with intermediate/poor-risk advanced renal-cell carcinoma (RCC) with a clear-cell component.
Treatment of advanced melanoma in adults in an NCCP-listed indication.

treatment.schedule_summary: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV then ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV every 21 days for 4 cycles. CRC: from cycle 5, nivolumab 240 mg IV every 14 days, 600 mg SC every 14 days or 1200 mg SC every 28 days, starting 3 weeks after the last combination dose. RCC/melanoma also have a 480 mg IV every 28 days option; first maintenance is 3 weeks after combination for a 14-day schedule or 6 weeks for a 28-day schedule. Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

eligibility: Confirm the exact source indication, treatment line and any biomarker requirements.
Adequate haematological, renal and hepatic function; the source does not specify numeric initiation cutoffs.
Effective contraception during treatment and for at least 5 months after the last nivolumab dose.
ECOG 0–2 for CRC/RCC and 0–1 for melanoma.
Melanoma: nivolumab 3 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg is an unlicensed dosing posology in Ireland; the source requires the local unlicensed-use consent and governance pathway.
exclusions: Hypersensitivity to a component/excipient; symptomatic interstitial lung disease; pregnancy/breastfeeding.
Consult current NCCP guidance concerning prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy.
RCC: prior systemic treatment for advanced RCC is excluded.
monitoring: Baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile, blood glucose and thyroid function; melanoma also requires BRAF status.
Before each cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile, glucose and thyroid function. Cortisol as clinically indicated.
Monitor for immune-related adverse reactions during treatment and for at least 5 months after the last dose.
Disease assessment and any additional tests follow the supervising consultant’s treatment plan; no fixed scan interval is specified.
dose_modifications: No dose reduction/escalation recommended. Source-specific holds/permanent stops and consultant review apply.
CTCAE v4.0 grades are clinician-confirmed; laboratory ratios do not replace source grade/baseline assessment.
Both components held together during combination phase. Physiological hormone replacement alone does not imply immunosuppressive-dose exposure.
